title: Leaning Poles
logline: A crew raises a tall bamboo frame for a village festival, poles leaning against each other's tips until, all at once, the structure holds on its own, decorations hanging from a frame that itself stands only because nothing in it stands alone.
human_question: What does it take for many unstable things to become one stable thing?

premise.story: A village crew building a festival frame or gateway, a pandal, a lit archway, a temporary tower, against a fixed opening date, from raw poles to the finished, lit structure.
premise.place: A village temple ground during a seasonal festival.
premise.experience: The tension of a structure that should not stand and somehow does: poles steadied by hand, an argument about angles, and the exact moment the frame first holds itself up.

concept_links.why: The mutuality condition's own image: several sticks staying upright only by leaning against each other's tips, together with the text's care to say that not everything arising together supports everything else.
The same 'nothing stands alone' summary, read through an ordinary structure rather than through doctrine.

what_camera_could_observe: A first attempt and a correction
The moment the frame holds without hands on it
A pole tested and the frame's give and recovery
The finished structure lit at night
what_must_be_real: The crew's real skill, deadline pressure and pay; no staged collapse or manufactured crisis.

possible_arc.opening: A pile of raw poles on open ground.
possible_arc.turn: The frame is raised and, for a moment, everyone steps back to see if it holds.
possible_arc.ending_open: The finished structure lit for the festival, or however the real build actually goes.

requirements: A village crew building a festival structure from raw materials on site, not pre-fabricated
A fixed opening date to build toward
Safe filming positions during the raising

suggestions.name: A village temple ground during a local festival season
suggestions.why: Deliberately a smaller, local festival rather than a major national procession, to allow closer access to one crew's whole build.
suggestions.verify: A specific festival, crew and structure must be found and confirmed.

risks: Becoming a neat visual metaphor with a voice-over lecture
The build being staged or accelerated for the camera
drop_if: No crew will let the camera in during the actual build
The structure is pre-fabricated rather than raised on site

connections.note: Both work at a communal, epic scale, following many people's coordinated effort rather than one person's story.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
